Frontend pillar: Ship a conversation-first control room where chat is the main operator interface; Show evidence status, control health, export state, and exceptions in structured side panels tied to the conversation; Support conversational evidence-gap resolution that updates the visible state of the system; Support evidence workflows involving GitHub and other authenticated surfaces, including media evidence state when required. Project story: nanobots is no longer a general-purpose AI bot swarm product. It is now a Sprinto-first SOC 2 middleware system that collects evidence from GitHub and other authenticated surfaces, structures that evidence into control-oriented artifacts, continuously monitors control freshness and exceptions, and exports actionable updates back into Sprinto. The product’s main interface is a conversation-first control room that helps an operator assemble the 'provable middle' needed for compliance evidence while showing structured evidence, control, export, and exception state alongside the conversation.. Definition of done: A real operator can connect evidence sources, gather evidence, map it to Sprinto-relevant controls, export or update Sprinto, and see current sync and health state in the UI; The system continuously monitors control freshness and exceptions after export instead of behaving like a one-shot uploader; The conversation interface can identify missing evidence, guide the user through gap closure, and materially change next actions or evidence state; Non-GitHub evidence capture works when the control requires it, including screenshot and/or video artifacts; Frontend and backend outcomes are both proven by unit/component tests and e2e tests; Roscoe must not call work done until pillars 3 and 4 prove pillars 1 and 2; Measured coverage for the new SOC 2 middleware scope is 100%, including expected behavior and edge cases, with a numeric coverage report produced from this repo. Frontend pillar: Ship a conversation-first control room where chat is the main operator interface; Show evidence status, control health, export state, and exceptions in structured side panels tied to the conversation; Support conversational evidence-gap resolution that updates the visible state of the system; Support evidence workflows involving GitHub and other authenticated surfaces, including media evidence state when required. Backend pillar: Implement evidence ingestion, normalization, control mapping, Sprinto export/update, and continuous monitoring as the core service contract; Support user-managed provider/API key configuration through the Vercel AI SDK-based system and do not reintroduce OpenRouter; Support browser/evidence collection jobs, durable evidence storage, and monitoring execution on the Kubernetes deployment model patterned after ~/Projects/node/k12io; Provide durable, trustworthy control-state and export-state handling with strong failure-mode behavior. Unit/component test pillar: Unit and component tests must cover 100% of expected behavior and edge cases for all new SOC 2 middleware codepaths; Those tests must prove the frontend and backend outcomes by covering evidence collectors, control mappers, export adapters, monitoring logic, provider-key handling, UI state transitions, and failure states; Roscoe must expand or replace the current Vitest coverage scope so it measures the new product paths such as src/app, src/components, src/lib/compliance, src/lib/chat, src/lib/db, and any new evidence-collection modules; Pillar 3 is a hard requirement, not supporting evidence; no task is done without this proof. Project story: nanobots is no longer a general-purpose AI bot swarm product. The product’s main interface is a conversation-first control room that helps an operator assemble the 'provable middle' needed for compliance evidence while showing structured evidence, control, export, and exception state alongside the conversation.. Definition of done: A real operator can connect evidence sources, gather evidence, map it to Sprinto-relevant controls, export or update Sprinto, and see current sync and health state in the UI; The system continuously monitors control freshness and exceptions after export instead of behaving like a one-shot uploader; The conversation interface can identify missing evidence, guide the user through gap closure, and materially change next actions or evidence state; Non-GitHub evidence capture works when the control requires it, including screenshot and/or video artifacts; Frontend and backend outcomes are both proven by unit/component tests and e2e tests; Roscoe must not call work done until pillars 3 and 4 prove pillars 1 and 2; Measured coverage for the new SOC 2 middleware scope is 100%, including expected behavior and edge cases, with a numeric coverage report produced from this repo. Acceptance checks: Roscoe must produce a measurable 100% coverage report for the new product scope; Roscoe must produce passing e2e proof of the full operator flow from authenticated entry through evidence collection, gap handling, export/update, and monitoring state; Roscoe must show visible proof that Sprinto export/update and monitoring status actually worked; Roscoe must show that a gap-resolution conversation changed the system’s next action or evidence state in a meaningful way; Roscoe must show that non-GitHub evidence capture worked when required, including screenshot/video artifacts; Roscoe must not rely on polished UI alone, happy-path backend demos alone, adapter/API tests alone, or GitHub-only evidence paths alone as proof of completion. Frontend pillar: Ship a conversation-first control room where chat is the main operator interface; Show evidence status, control health, export state, and exceptions in structured side panels tied to the conversation; Support conversational evidence-gap resolution that updates the visible state of the system; Support evidence workflows involving GitHub and other authenticated surfaces, including media evidence state when required. Backend pillar: Implement evidence ingestion, normalization, control mapping, Sprinto export/update, and continuous monitoring as the core service contract; Support user-managed provider/API key configuration through the Vercel AI SDK-based system and do not reintroduce OpenRouter; Support browser/evidence collection jobs, durable evidence storage, and monitoring execution on the Kubernetes deployment model patterned after ~/Projects/node/k12io; Provide durable, trustworthy control-state and export-state handling with strong failure-mode behavior. Project story: nanobots is no longer a general-purpose AI bot swarm product. The product’s main interface is a conversation-first control room that helps an operator assemble the 'provable middle' needed for compliance evidence while showing structured evidence, control, export, and exception state alongside the conversation.. Definition of done: A real operator can connect evidence sources, gather evidence, map it to Sprinto-relevant controls, export or update Sprinto, and see current sync and health state in the UI; The system continuously monitors control freshness and exceptions after export instead of behaving like a one-shot uploader; The conversation interface can identify missing evidence, guide the user through gap closure, and materially change next actions or evidence state; Non-GitHub evidence capture works when the control requires it, including screenshot and/or video artifacts; Frontend and backend outcomes are both proven by unit/component tests and e2e tests; Roscoe must not call work done until pillars 3 and 4 prove pillars 1 and 2; Measured coverage for the new SOC 2 middleware scope is 100%, including expected behavior and edge cases, with a numeric coverage report produced from this repo. Acceptance checks: Roscoe must produce a measurable 100% coverage report for the new product scope; Roscoe must produce passing e2e proof of the full operator flow from authenticated entry through evidence collection, gap handling, export/update, and monitoring state; Roscoe must show visible proof that Sprinto export/update and monitoring status actually worked; Roscoe must show that a gap-resolution conversation changed the system’s next action or evidence state in a meaningful way; Roscoe must show that non-GitHub evidence capture worked when required, including screenshot/video artifacts; Roscoe must not rely on polished UI alone, happy-path backend demos alone, adapter/API tests alone, or GitHub-only evidence paths alone as proof of completion. Frontend pillar: Ship a conversation-first control room where chat is the main operator interface; Show evidence status, control health, export state, and exceptions in structured side panels tied to the conversation; Support conversational evidence-gap resolution that updates the visible state of the system; Support evidence workflows involving GitHub and other authenticated surfaces, including media evidence state when required. Backend pillar: Implement evidence ingestion, normalization, control mapping, Sprinto export/update, and continuous monitoring as the core service contract; Support user-managed provider/API key configuration through the Vercel AI SDK-based system and do not reintroduce OpenRouter; Support browser/evidence collection jobs, durable evidence storage, and monitoring execution on the Kubernetes deployment model patterned after ~/Projects/node/k12io; Provide durable, trustworthy control-state and export-state handling with strong failure-mode behavior. Project story: nanobots is no longer a general-purpose AI bot swarm product. The product’s main interface is a conversation-first control room that helps an operator assemble the 'provable middle' needed for compliance evidence while showing structured evidence, control, export, and exception state alongside the conversation.. Definition of done: A real operator can connect evidence sources, gather evidence, map it to Sprinto-relevant controls, export or update Sprinto, and see current sync and health state in the UI; The system continuously monitors control freshness and exceptions after export instead of behaving like a one-shot uploader; The conversation interface can identify missing evidence, guide the user through gap closure, and materially change next actions or evidence state; Non-GitHub evidence capture works when the control requires it, including screenshot and/or video artifacts; Frontend and backend outcomes are both proven by unit/component tests and e2e tests; Roscoe must not call work done until pillars 3 and 4 prove pillars 1 and 2; Measured coverage for the new SOC 2 middleware scope is 100%, including expected behavior and edge cases, with a numeric coverage report produced from this repo. Acceptance checks: Roscoe must produce a measurable 100% coverage report for the new product scope; Roscoe must produce passing e2e proof of the full operator flow from authenticated entry through evidence collection, gap handling, export/update, and monitoring state; Roscoe must show visible proof that Sprinto export/update and monitoring status actually worked; Roscoe must show that a gap-resolution conversation changed the system’s next action or evidence state in a meaningful way; Roscoe must show that non-GitHub evidence capture worked when required, including screenshot/video artifacts; Roscoe must not rely on polished UI alone, happy-path backend demos alone, adapter/API tests alone, or GitHub-only evidence paths alone as proof of completion. Frontend pillar: Ship a conversation-first control room where chat is the main operator interface; Show evidence status, control health, export state, and exceptions in structured side panels tied to the conversation; Support conversational evidence-gap resolution that updates the visible state of the system; Support evidence workflows involving GitHub and other authenticated surfaces, including media evidence state when required. Backend pillar: Implement evidence ingestion, normalization, control mapping, Sprinto export/update, and continuous monitoring as the core service contract; Support user-managed provider/API key configuration through the Vercel AI SDK-based system and do not reintroduce OpenRouter; Support browser/evidence collection jobs, durable evidence storage, and monitoring execution on the Kubernetes deployment model patterned after ~/Projects/node/k12io; Provide durable, trustworthy control-state and export-state handling with strong failure-mode behavior. Project story: nanobots is no longer a general-purpose AI bot swarm product. The product’s main interface is a conversation-first control room that helps an operator assemble the 'provable middle' needed for compliance evidence while showing structured evidence, control, export, and exception state alongside the conversation.. Definition of done: A real operator can connect evidence sources, gather evidence, map it to Sprinto-relevant controls, export or update Sprinto, and see current sync and health state in the UI; The system continuously monitors control freshness and exceptions after export instead of behaving like a one-shot uploader; The conversation interface can identify missing evidence, guide the user through gap closure, and materially change next actions or evidence state; Non-GitHub evidence capture works when the control requires it, including screenshot and/or video artifacts; Frontend and backend outcomes are both proven by unit/component tests and e2e tests; Roscoe must not call work done until pillars 3 and 4 prove pillars 1 and 2; Measured coverage for the new SOC 2 middleware scope is 100%, including expected behavior and edge cases, with a numeric coverage report produced from this repo. Acceptance checks: Roscoe must produce a measurable 100% coverage report for the new product scope; Roscoe must produce passing e2e proof of the full operator flow from authenticated entry through evidence collection, gap handling, export/update, and monitoring state; Roscoe must show visible proof that Sprinto export/update and monitoring status actually worked; Roscoe must show that a gap-resolution conversation changed the system’s next action or evidence state in a meaningful way; Roscoe must show that non-GitHub evidence capture worked when required, including screenshot/video artifacts; Roscoe must not rely on polished UI alone, happy-path backend demos alone, adapter/API tests alone, or GitHub-only evidence paths alone as proof of completion. Frontend pillar: Ship a conversation-first control room where chat is the main operator interface; Show evidence status, control health, export state, and exceptions in structured side panels tied to the conversation; Support conversational evidence-gap resolution that updates the visible state of the system; Support evidence workflows involving GitHub and other authenticated surfaces, including media evidence state when required. Backend pillar: Implement evidence ingestion, normalization, control mapping, Sprinto export/update, and continuous monitoring as the core service contract; Support user-managed provider/API key configuration through the Vercel AI SDK-based system and do not reintroduce OpenRouter; Support browser/evidence collection jobs, durable evidence storage, and monitoring execution on the Kubernetes deployment model patterned after ~/Projects/node/k12io; Provide durable, trustworthy control-state and export-state handling with strong failure-mode behavior. Project story: nanobots is no longer a general-purpose AI bot swarm product. The product’s main interface is a conversation-first control room that helps an operator assemble the 'provable middle' needed for compliance evidence while showing structured evidence, control, export, and exception state alongside the conversation.. Definition of done: A real operator can connect evidence sources, gather evidence, map it to Sprinto-relevant controls, export or update Sprinto, and see current sync and health state in the UI; The system continuously monitors control freshness and exceptions after export instead of behaving like a one-shot uploader; The conversation interface can identify missing evidence, guide the user through gap closure, and materially change next actions or evidence state; Non-GitHub evidence capture works when the control requires it, including screenshot and/or video artifacts; Frontend and backend outcomes are both proven by unit/component tests and e2e tests; Roscoe must not call work done until pillars 3 and 4 prove pillars 1 and 2; Measured coverage for the new SOC 2 middleware scope is 100%, including expected behavior and edge cases, with a numeric coverage report produced from this repo. Acceptance checks: Roscoe must produce a measurable 100% coverage report for the new product scope; Roscoe must produce passing e2e proof of the full operator flow from authenticated entry through evidence collection, gap handling, export/update, and monitoring state; Roscoe must show visible proof that Sprinto export/update and monitoring status actually worked; Roscoe must show that a gap-resolution conversation changed the system’s next action or evidence state in a meaningful way; Roscoe must show that non-GitHub evidence capture worked when required, including screenshot/video artifacts; Roscoe must not rely on polished UI alone, happy-path backend demos alone, adapter/API tests alone, or GitHub-only evidence paths alone as proof of completion. Frontend pillar: Ship a conversation-first control room where chat is the main operator interface; Show evidence status, control health, export state, and exceptions in structured side panels tied to the conversation; Support conversational evidence-gap resolution that updates the visible state of the system; Support evidence workflows involving GitHub and other authenticated surfaces, including media evidence state when required. Backend pillar: Implement evidence ingestion, normalization, control mapping, Sprinto export/update, and continuous monitoring as the core service contract; Support user-managed provider/API key configuration through the Vercel AI SDK-based system and do not reintroduce OpenRouter; Support browser/evidence collection jobs, durable evidence storage, and monitoring execution on the Kubernetes deployment model patterned after ~/Projects/node/k12io; Provide durable, trustworthy control-state and export-state handling with strong failure-mode behavior. Project story: nanobots is no longer a general-purpose AI bot swarm product. The product’s main interface is a conversation-first control room that helps an operator assemble the 'provable middle' needed for compliance evidence while showing structured evidence, control, export, and exception state alongside the conversation.. Definition of done: A real operator can connect evidence sources, gather evidence, map it to Sprinto-relevant controls, export or update Sprinto, and see current sync and health state in the UI; The system continuously monitors control freshness and exceptions after export instead of behaving like a one-shot uploader; The conversation interface can identify missing evidence, guide the user through gap closure, and materially change next actions or evidence state; Non-GitHub evidence capture works when the control requires it, including screenshot and/or video artifacts; Frontend and backend outcomes are both proven by unit/component tests and e2e tests; Roscoe must not call work done until pillars 3 and 4 prove pillars 1 and 2; Measured coverage for the new SOC 2 middleware scope is 100%, including expected behavior and edge cases, with a numeric coverage report produced from this repo. Acceptance checks: Roscoe must produce a measurable 100% coverage report for the new product scope; Roscoe must produce passing e2e proof of the full operator flow from authenticated entry through evidence collection, gap handling, export/update, and monitoring state; Roscoe must show visible proof that Sprinto export/update and monitoring status actually worked; Roscoe must show that a gap-resolution conversation changed the system’s next action or evidence state in a meaningful way; Roscoe must show that non-GitHub evidence capture worked when required, including screenshot/video artifacts; Roscoe must not rely on polished UI alone, happy-path backend demos alone, adapter/API tests alone, or GitHub-only evidence paths alone as proof of completion. Frontend pillar: Ship a conversation-first control room where chat is the main operator interface; Show evidence status, control health, export state, and exceptions in structured side panels tied to the conversation; Support conversational evidence-gap resolution that updates the visible state of the system; Support evidence workflows involving GitHub and other authenticated surfaces, including media evidence state when required. Backend pillar: Implement evidence ingestion, normalization, control mapping, Sprinto export/update, and continuous monitoring as the core service contract; Support user-managed provider/API key configuration through the Vercel AI SDK-based system and do not reintroduce OpenRouter; Support browser/evidence collection jobs, durable evidence storage, and monitoring execution on the Kubernetes deployment model patterned after ~/Projects/node/k12io; Provide durable, trustworthy control-state and export-state handling with strong failure-mode behavior.
